title: Anti-Wrinkle Injections
tagline: Smooth, refresh and subtly lift — with expert precision
intro: Anti-wrinkle injections are one of the most popular non-surgical treatments available, used to soften facial lines and wrinkles while preserving natural expression. At YourHealthFirst, every treatment is carefully tailored to your facial anatomy and aesthetic goals.
benefits: Reverses the signs of ageing and dramatically diminishes the appearance of wrinkles
Relaxes the facial muscles, resulting in smoother skin and fewer wrinkles

Provides a more fresh, rested and youthful appearance

Slims the jawline by relaxing the masseter muscles

faqs.question: How many treatments will I need?
faqs.answer: You only need one session per treatment to see results, and it might need a top up after 2 weeks. However, because Botox is a temporary treatment, you will need maintenance sessions every 4 to 6 months to maintain your results.

faqs.question: What results can I expect?
faqs.answer: A softened, more rested appearance in the treated area with your natural expression preserved. Dr Sofia's approach favours subtle, natural movement rather than a 'frozen' look, so you'll still be able to smile, frown and raise your brows normally.

faqs.question: Will it 'freeze' my face and leave me expressionless?
faqs.answer: No. When dosed and placed correctly, anti-wrinkle injections relax only the specific muscles causing the lines you want softened, while surrounding muscles continue to move naturally. This is why precise placement, not just the product itself, is what determines a natural result.

faqs.question: What are the side-effects?
faqs.answer: Mild redness, small bumps at the injection sites, or slight bruising can occur and typically settle within a day or two. Headache is occasionally reported after forehead treatment. Serious side effects are rare when performed by an experienced practitioner.

faqs.question: Is the treatment painful?
faqs.answer: Most patients describe it as a series of quick, small pinpricks rather than pain. The needles used are very fine, and the whole treatment for a typical area takes only a few minutes.

faqs.question: How long will it last?
faqs.answer: Results generally last 3–6 months depending on the area treated, your muscle strength and your individual metabolism. Areas like hyperhidrosis treatment can last up to 6–9 months.

faqs.question: What can't I do after the treatment?
faqs.answer: Avoid touching, rubbing, or massaging the treated area for at least 24 hours to prevent the Botox from spreading to unintended muscles.

faqs.question: Who is suitable for anti-wrinkle injections?
faqs.answer: Most healthy adults concerned about dynamic lines, jaw clenching, gummy smiles or excessive sweating are good candidates. Pregnant or breastfeeding women, and those with certain neuromuscular conditions, are not suitable — this is confirmed during your consultation.

faqs.question: Does it leave my face numb?
faqs.answer: No. Anti-wrinkle injections relax the targeted muscles but don't affect sensation — your skin remains fully able to feel touch, temperature and pressure as normal.

faqs.question: When will I notice a difference?
faqs.answer: Most patients begin to see softening within 3–5 days, with the full effect visible by day 14. If an area still looks under-treated after 2 weeks, a top-up can be arranged.

faqs.question: How will I look after the treatment?
faqs.answer: You may have small bumps or slight redness at the injection points for a few hours, which settles quickly. There is no visible downtime, so most patients return straight to work or normal activities.

faqs.question: How does anti-wrinkle treatment work?
faqs.answer: Botulinum toxin is injected into specific facial muscles, temporarily blocking the nerve signals that cause them to contract. With the muscle at rest, the skin above it smooths out and existing lines soften over the following days.

faqs.question: Is it safe?
faqs.answer: Yes, when performed by an experienced, appropriately qualified practitioner using licensed products. Sofia carries out a full medical assessment at consultation to confirm suitability and agree the right dose and placement for you.

faqs.question: What is anti-wrinkle treatment used for?
faqs.answer: Beyond softening forehead, frown and crow's feet lines, it's also used for a non-surgical brow lift, jawline slimming, gummy smile correction and treating excessive sweating (hyperhidrosis) in the underarms, palms or feet.

faqs.question: How many sessions will I need?
faqs.answer: Most filler treatments achieve their full result in a single session. Some patients choose a follow-up appointment 2–4 weeks later for minor fine-tuning once any initial swelling has settled.

faqs.question: What results can I expect?
faqs.answer: Immediate, visible volume restoration or contouring in the treated area — for example plumper lips, softened nasolabial folds, or a smoother under-eye area. Results continue to settle and look even more natural over the following 1–2 weeks.

faqs.question: Will I look overfilled or unnatural?
faqs.answer: No — Dr Sofia's approach prioritises symmetry, proportion and a natural outcome over maximum volume. Filler is built up gradually and conservatively, and dissolving is always available if you ever want a correction.

faqs.question: What are the side-effects?
faqs.answer: Temporary swelling, bruising or tenderness at the injection site is common and usually resolves within a few days to a week. Lips in particular can swell noticeably for the first 24–48 hours.

faqs.question: Is the treatment painful?
faqs.answer: A topical numbing cream is applied before treatment in sensitive areas such as the lips, and most fillers contain a local anaesthetic within the product itself, making the procedure very tolerable for most patients.

faqs.question: How long will it last?
faqs.answer: Depending on the area and product used, results typically last 9–18 months. Lips tend to metabolise filler faster (6–12 months), while structural areas like cheeks and jawline can last longer.

faqs.question: What should I do and avoid after treatment?
faqs.answer: Avoid strenuous exercise, alcohol and excessive heat (saunas, sunbeds) for 24–48 hours, and avoid pressing on or massaging the treated area unless instructed to. Mild swelling is normal and settles within a few days.

faqs.question: Who is suitable for dermal fillers?
faqs.answer: Adults with volume loss, hollowing or asymmetry seeking a non-surgical improvement are generally suitable. A full medical history is taken at consultation to rule out any contraindications before treatment.

faqs.question: What are dermal fillers made of?
faqs.answer: Most fillers used at YourHealthFirst are hyaluronic acid-based — a substance naturally found in the skin — chosen for their effective, natural-looking results and because they can be dissolved if needed. Collagen, fat-based and other synthetic fillers exist, but hyaluronic acid remains the most widely used and best-suited option for the majority of patients.

faqs.question: What are the possible lip filler side-effects?
faqs.answer: The most common side-effects are swelling, tenderness, bruising and slight lumpiness at the injection site, which typically settle within a few days to a week — lips in particular can look noticeably swollen for the first 24–48 hours. Less commonly, patients may experience cold-sore flare-ups, asymmetry that needs a top-up, or a very rare allergic reaction or vascular complication, which is why a full medical history and an experienced injector matter.

intro: Sunekos is an injectable treatment combining amino acids and hyaluronic acid to stimulate the skin's own production of collagen and elastin. It is suitable for the face, neck, décolleté and hands, delivering a naturally plumped, firmer and more luminous complexion.

faqs.question: What is Sunekos?
faqs.answer: Sunekos is an injectable treatment containing amino acids and hyaluronic acid. It works by stimulating the fibroblasts in the skin to produce collagen and elastin, and has been proven very safe with no contraindications for most patients — it can be used on all skin types.

faqs.question: How many sessions will I need?
faqs.answer: A standard course is 4 sessions spaced 7–10 days apart. This spacing allows the amino acid and hyaluronic acid formula to progressively stimulate fibroblast activity for a build-up effect.

faqs.question: What results can I expect?
faqs.answer: Firmer, more hydrated and more luminous skin with a visible reduction in fine lines and crepiness. Because Sunekos works by stimulating your own collagen and elastin, the improvement looks structural rather than 'filled'.

faqs.question: When will I notice a difference?
faqs.answer: Skin hydration and glow are often noticeable after the first session, with firmness and elasticity continuing to improve for several weeks after the full course is complete.

faqs.question: What are the side-effects?
faqs.answer: Mild redness or small bumps at the injection points are common immediately after treatment and typically settle within a few hours to a day.

faqs.question: Is the treatment painful?
faqs.answer: Sunekos is injected using very fine needles across the treatment area. Most patients tolerate it well, describing only mild discomfort, particularly in more delicate areas like under the eyes.

faqs.question: How long will results last?
faqs.answer: Results from a full course typically last 6–9 months, after which a maintenance session every 3–6 months is recommended to sustain the improvement.

faqs.question: Can Sunekos be used on younger skin preventatively?
faqs.answer: Yes — Sunekos is popular with patients from age 25 onwards as a way to maintain skin quality and delay early signs of ageing, not just to correct existing damage.

faqs.question: Who is suitable for Sunekos?
faqs.answer: Anyone with loss of elasticity, dullness, crepey skin or early fine lines on the face, neck, décolleté or hands. It is also suitable for younger patients wanting preventative skin maintenance.

faqs.question: Is Sunekos a filler?
faqs.answer: No — Sunekos is not a dermal filler. While it contains hyaluronic acid like traditional fillers, it works differently: it stimulates your own fibroblasts to regenerate collagen and elastin through a process called dermal biogenesis, essentially triggering your skin to regenerate itself rather than simply adding volume.

faqs.question: What is Sunekos eye treatment used for?
faqs.answer: Sunekos can be used around the eye area to help reduce dark circles by thickening the skin, and its elastin-stimulating effect can help reduce the appearance of eye bags and hollowness.

faqs.question: How long does the appointment take?
faqs.answer: The treatment itself takes around 30 minutes.

faqs.question: Who should not be treated with Sunekos?
faqs.answer: Sunekos should not be used on patients who are pregnant or breastfeeding, those with a history of severe allergies or anaphylaxis, or patients with a compromised immune system. Dr Sofia will confirm suitability at your consultation.

faqs.question: What should I expect from the treatment?
faqs.answer: Patients typically benefit from a lifting and tightening effect, reduced volume loss, reduced wrinkle severity, improved deep and surface skin hydration, and improved facial definition.

faqs.answer: Polynucleotides work by stimulating the skin's own regeneration processes — boosting collagen production and hydration at a cellular level. This repairs damaged tissue, improving skin elasticity and the overall health of skin and hair.

faqs.question: What areas can be treated with Polynucleotides?

faqs.question: Who is a good candidate for Polynucleotide treatment?
faqs.answer: Polynucleotides are ideal for anyone wanting to improve skin texture, reduce signs of ageing or improve hair health — including those with fine lines, wrinkles or sagging skin, dull or dehydrated skin, thinning hair or weak follicles, and anyone seeking a natural, non-invasive rejuvenation option.

faqs.question: How soon can I see results from Polynucleotide therapy?

faqs.question: How long do the results last?

faqs.question: How soon will I notice results?

faqs.question: How long does Sculptra last?

faqs.question: What should I expect during treatment?
faqs.answer: Each session takes about 30–45 minutes. Some redness or bruising is normal and fades quickly; an ice pack can help with any discomfort.

faqs.question: How safe is Sculptra?
faqs.answer: Sculptra's active ingredient, poly-L-lactic acid (PLA), is biocompatible, fully absorbable, and has a long track record of safe use in medicine — including suture thread and orthopaedic pins and screws. No skin test is required before treatment.

faqs.question: Will the injections hurt?
faqs.answer: Sculptra contains a built-in local anaesthetic, lidocaine. You may feel a slight sting as it's injected, but there's usually little to no discomfort afterwards.

faqs.question: How many sessions will I need?
faqs.answer: Most patients need 2–3 sessions spaced roughly 6 weeks apart, allowing each round of collagen stimulation to build on the last.

faqs.question: What's the difference between Sculptra and dermal fillers?
faqs.answer: Sculptra uses poly-L-lactic acid to replace lost collagen rather than simply adding volume, so its effects build gradually and subtly replenish volume over time — and results can last up to two years, longer than most traditional fillers.

faqs.question: Why does it take longer to see results than fillers?
faqs.answer: Because Sculptra doesn't add volume directly — it stimulates your own body to gradually produce new collagen over 3–6 months, which is why the result builds slowly and looks so natural.

faqs.question: What are the side-effects?
faqs.answer: Swelling, redness and small bumps at injection sites are common initially and usually settle within days. Very occasionally, small nodules can form under the skin, which is why post-treatment massage is important.

faqs.question: How long will results last?
faqs.answer: Results can last up to 2 years or more, making Sculptra one of the longer-lasting options among facial volumising treatments.

faqs.question: Who is suitable for Sculptra?
faqs.answer: Adults with significant facial volume loss who want a subtle, progressive improvement rather than an immediate dramatic change, and who are looking for a longer-lasting result from fewer overall sessions.

faqs.question: How long does Sculptra take to work?
faqs.answer: Sculptra works gradually. Improvements typically develop over several weeks to months as collagen production increases. The timing and extent of results vary between individuals.

faqs.question: How long do Sculptra results last?
faqs.answer: Clinical studies and product information report that results may last up to two years or longer in some patients. Longevity varies depending on individual factors and the treatment plan.

faqs.question: Is Sculptra the same as dermal filler?
faqs.answer: No. Sculptra is a collagen-stimulating injectable containing poly-L-lactic acid, whereas many conventional dermal fillers contain hyaluronic acid and provide more immediate volume. Your practitioner can explain which approach is appropriate for your treatment goals.

faqs.question: Does Sculptra give an instant facelift?
faqs.answer: No. Sculptra is not a surgical facelift or an instant lifting treatment. It works progressively and is intended to improve facial volume and contours over time.

faqs.question: Is there scientific evidence for this treatment?

faqs.question: Why is PRFM superior to standard PRP?
faqs.answer: PRFM requires only around 4 sessions to see a visible result. Its sustained release, continuing for up to 7 days after the procedure, allows cell angiogenesis and hair regrowth in the scalp, and it increases hair density and thickness almost 2 times within 6 months.

faqs.question: How does this compare to other hair loss treatments?
faqs.answer: PRF matrix releases growth factors into the scalp through a sustained mechanism — in vitro studies have shown growth factors are released for up to 7 days, which stimulates new hair growth. Pronounced results are typically seen after 3 months of treatment.

faqs.question: What is PRFM (Platelet-Rich Fibrin Matrix)?
faqs.answer: PRFM is considered one of the latest innovations in hair treatment. This matrix is then injected into the thinning or bald scalp, stimulating cell proliferation and hair regrowth through targeted tissue regeneration.

faqs.question: How long does the appointment take?

faqs.question: Is PRP safe?
faqs.answer: PRP is an especially safe treatment option with no risk of allergic reaction, because it is made from your own blood. As it's antimicrobial, there is also no risk of infection.

faqs.question: Is PRP good for hair loss?
faqs.answer: PRP has been studied as a treatment for androgenetic alopecia, with research suggesting potential improvements in hair density in some patients. Results vary and treatment is not guaranteed.

faqs.question: Can PRP regrow hair?
faqs.answer: PRP may support hair density and follicle activity in suitable patients, particularly in androgenetic alopecia. It is not a guaranteed method of restoring hair where follicles are permanently inactive or destroyed.

faqs.question: Is PRP suitable for men and women?
faqs.answer: Yes. PRP has been studied in both male and female pattern hair loss, although the treatment plan should be individualised.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Standard PRP and PRP Cellular Matrix + Biotin?
faqs.answer: Standard PRP uses platelet-rich plasma prepared from your own blood and is manually administered. PRP Cellular Matrix + Biotin is an advanced clinic treatment protocol combining PRP with a Cellular Matrix approach and Biotin, with U225-assisted administration where appropriate.

faqs.question: Can PRP stop hair loss permanently?
faqs.answer: PRP should not be marketed as a permanent cure for hair loss. Hair-loss conditions can continue to progress, and ongoing management may be required.

faqs.question: Is cryolipolysis painful?

faqs.question: What are the side-effects?

faqs.question: What about frostbite?
faqs.answer: Cryolipolysis temperatures are not cold enough to cause frostbite or other skin damage — that requires temperatures of around -10°C. Cryolipolysis uses controlled temperatures that don't immediately destroy the fat cells, but rather trigger the natural process of cell death (apoptosis), and a special anti-freezing membrane protects the skin throughout treatment.

faqs.question: Is cryolipolysis permanent?
faqs.answer: Yes — cryolipolysis eliminates the treated fat cells permanently and they do not come back. If you gain weight afterwards, any remaining fat cells can still grow, so maintaining a good diet and exercise regimen helps you enjoy lasting results.

faqs.question: Does the fat come back afterwards?
faqs.answer: No — the destroyed fat cells are permanently eliminated by the body and do not regenerate. Maintaining a stable weight afterwards ensures the results are sustained long-term.

faqs.question: When will I see results?
faqs.answer: The body gradually clears the destroyed fat cells over several weeks. Initial results are visible from around 8 weeks, with the optimal outcome seen at 12–16 weeks.

faqs.question: Can multiple areas be treated at once?
faqs.answer: Yes — depending on your goals, multiple applicators and areas can be treated within the same appointment, which Dr Sofia will plan with you at consultation.

faqs.question: Who is suitable for cryolipolysis?
faqs.answer: Adults at or near their ideal body weight with stubborn, diet-and-exercise-resistant fat pockets in specific areas. It is not a weight-loss treatment for those significantly overweight.

faqs.question: How do I prepare for cryolipolysis treatment?

faqs.question: What are the side-effects?
faqs.answer: Most commonly reported side effects are gastrointestinal — nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, constipation, abdominal discomfort and reduced appetite — and can be more noticeable when treatment is started or the dose is increased. faqs.question: Is the injection painful?

faqs.question: When will I see results?

body.heading: The Dawn of Regenerative Aesthetics
paragraphs: Aesthetic medicine is undergoing a profound paradigm shift. Where traditional treatments historically focused on artificial volume expansion or surgical excision, modern patients increasingly demand natural, biostimulatory solutions that repair tissue at the cellular level.

Platelet-Rich Plasma (PRP) and Exosome therapy stand at the forefront of this revolution. By uniting autologous growth factors with nano-engineered biological messengers, we are able to trigger deep rejuvenation across the scalp, face, and body with superior clinical precision.

body.heading: Understanding Platelet-Rich Plasma (PRP)
paragraphs: PRP begins with a gentle blood draw performed by a qualified phlebotomist at our London clinic. Using patented medical centrifuge technology (such as Regen Lab closed-circuit systems), red blood cells and granulocytes are separated out, isolating an enriched plasma suspension loaded with concentrated platelets.
When activated in target tissues, these platelets release powerful bioactive growth factors, including:
bullets: Platelet-Derived Growth Factor (PDGF) — stimulates cell proliferation and angiogenesis (new capillary growth).
Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor (VEGF) — expands blood circulation around hair follicles and dermal layers.

Epidermal Growth Factor (EGF) — drives cellular turnover and healthy skin epidermal repair.

body.heading: What Are Exosomes and Why Are They Revolutionary?

In tissue regeneration, exosomes communicate directly with recipient fibroblasts and dermal papilla stem cells, delivering the exact biochemical instructions needed to ramp up collagen synthesis, calm chronic low-grade inflammation, and reignite dormant cellular cycles.

paragraphs: At YourHealthFirst Clinic, we tailor dual PRP + Exosome protocols across three primary treatment indications:
bullets: Hair Restoration: In androgenetic alopecia, telogen effluvium, and traction hair thinning, the combination reactivates miniaturized follicles, thickens hair shaft caliber, and extends the active growth (anagen) phase.

title: Anti-Wrinkle Injections — Everything You Need to Know
excerpt: Anti-wrinkle injections remain one of the most requested aesthetic treatments in the UK. Dr. Sofia covers what they are, how they work, the areas treated, and what creates the difference between a natural look and an overdone appearance.
keyTakeaways: Temporarily relaxes facial hyperactive muscles to smooth dynamic expression lines.
Prevents dynamic lines from becoming permanently etched static creases over time.
Dr. Sofia’s philosophy prioritizes natural facial animation — smoothing lines while preserving your true expression.
Advanced therapeutic uses include masseter jawline slimming, bruxism relief, and hyperhidrosis (sweating) control.

body.heading: The Science of Dynamic vs. Static Wrinkles
paragraphs: Every day, our faces make thousands of micro-expressions — smiling, frowning, squinting, and concentrating. In youth, high levels of elastin and collagen allow skin to snap back seamlessly.

As natural dermal support declines with age, the repetitive muscle contractions cause 'dynamic wrinkles'. Left unaddressed, these fold repeatedly along the same creases, eventually becoming permanent 'static wrinkles' visible even when your face is at complete rest.

body.heading: How Anti-Wrinkle Injections Work
paragraphs: Anti-wrinkle injections utilize purified botulinum neuroprotein type A. When micro-injected with ultrafine needles into precise muscle targets, the solution temporarily blocks acetylcholine neurotransmitters from signaling muscle contraction.
The overlying skin relaxes, allowing established wrinkles to smooth out and preventing new creases from forming.

body.heading: Primary Cosmetic & Therapeutic Treatment Zones
paragraphs: At our London clinic, treatments are strictly customized to your unique muscular anatomy:
bullets: The Upper Face Trio: Forehead horizontal lines, glabella frown lines ('11s'), and crow's feet around the eyes.
Brow Lift: Subtly lifting the tail of the eyebrow to open and brighten tired eyes.
Bunny Lines: Softening horizontal wrinkles across the bridge of the nose.
Gummy Smile: Relaxing the levator labii muscles so the upper lip does not over-retract when smiling.
Masseter Slimming & Bruxism: Relaxing the jaw clenching muscle to alleviate teeth grinding and sculpt a softer jawline.
Hyperhidrosis: Blocking sweat gland nerve signals in the underarms for 6+ months of dryness.

body.heading: The Harley Street Natural Aesthetic
paragraphs: One of the biggest concerns patients voice is the fear of looking 'frozen' or unnatural. Dr. Sofia’s micro-dosing technique ensures that key retaining muscles maintain mobility, preserving warm eye smiles and natural brow inflection.

Results begin developing within 3 to 5 days, with the full refined outcome visible at day 14. Longevity typically ranges between 3 and 5 months, with regular treatments often extending the intervals between top-ups.

faqs.question: Will my face look frozen?
faqs.answer: Not under Dr. Sofia's care. We practice a conservative, anatomy-led technique designed to smooth wrinkles while retaining your authentic facial expressions and warmth.

faqs.question: How long does the appointment take?
faqs.answer: The injection portion takes only 10 to 15 minutes, earning it the reputation of the ultimate 'lunchtime treatment'. You can return immediately to your daily schedule.

faqs.question: What is the crucial aftercare advice?
faqs.answer: Keep your head upright for 4 hours post-treatment. Avoid strenuous workouts, saunas, hot tubs, and alcohol for 24 hours to ensure optimal product uptake.

title: PRP for Hair Loss — A Complete Guide
excerpt: Platelet-Rich Plasma therapy for hair loss is backed by extensive clinical evidence. This guide explains how autologous growth factors reverse follicular miniaturization, how many sessions are needed, and how PRP compares to other therapies.
keyTakeaways: Autologous platelets release concentrated cytokines directly into the scalp micro-environment.
Reverses follicular miniaturization and transitions dormant follicles back into active growth.
Zero risk of allergic or foreign-body reactions since the treatment is 100% autologous.
Significantly outperforms generic topical solutions when performed with medical-grade centrifugation.

body.heading: The Modern Epidemic of Hair Thinning
paragraphs: Thinning hair is not merely a cosmetic concern; it deeply affects self-image and daily confidence. Today, hair loss touches younger demographics than ever before due to hormonal fluctuations, chronic stress, environmental factors, and genetics.

In the past, patients felt trapped between lifelong daily medication or invasive hair transplant surgery. PRP has bridged this gap, offering a scientifically validated biological therapy that reactivates your natural hair growth cycle.

body.heading: How Platelets Stimulate the Hair Cycle
paragraphs: Human hair grows in cycles: Anagen (active growth, 2–7 years), Catagen (transition, 2–3 weeks), and Telogen (resting/shedding, 3 months). In patterned hair loss, the anagen phase progressively shortens while telogen lengthens.
When concentrated platelets are introduced into the scalp dermis, they release PDGF, VEGF, and IGF-1. These biochemical triggers:
bullets: Prolong the Anagen phase, keeping hair in active production longer.
Increase the diameter of miniaturized hair shafts, creating denser visual coverage.
Upregulate local micro-capillary networks, delivering oxygen and amino acids directly to the follicle.

body.heading: Comparing PRP to Traditional Alternatives
paragraphs: Understanding where PRP fits among hair loss solutions helps patients make informed decisions:
bullets: Versus Minoxidil: PRP requires periodic clinical sessions rather than daily lifelong messy topical application, and avoids scalp dermatitis.
Versus Oral Finasteride: PRP is completely local and autologous, eliminating concerns over systemic hormonal disruption.
Versus Hair Transplant Surgery: PRP requires zero surgical excision, zero linear scarring, and zero prolonged healing. It also serves as ideal maintenance around transplanted grafts.

body.heading: The Recommended Treatment Course
paragraphs: Hair biology operates on a 3-month physiological cycle. Consequently, sustainable results require a structured medical protocol:
bullets: Month 1: Initial priming session to halt active hair shedding.
Month 2: Second session to stimulate follicle vascularization.
Month 3: Third session to trigger robust anagen growth.
Maintenance: One session every 6 to 9 months preserves and compounds the density gains.

faqs.question: Can women undergo PRP hair treatment?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. In fact, PRP is one of the most effective treatments for female diffuse thinning, postpartum hair loss, and female pattern hair loss where oral medications are contraindicated.

faqs.question: How should I prepare for my PRP appointment?
faqs.answer: Drink plenty of water in the 24 hours prior to your visit to ensure optimal blood hydration, and wash your hair thoroughly on the morning of your procedure.

faqs.question: Does PRP work on completely bald scalp areas?
faqs.answer: PRP requires the presence of viable, miniaturized hair follicles. If an area has been completely smooth and bald for many years, surgical transplantation may be necessary, complemented by PRP to support surrounding zones.

title: Dermal Fillers and Their Uses — The Complete Guide
excerpt: From lip enhancement to non-surgical rhinoplasty, dermal fillers have a remarkably wide range of applications. Dr. Sofia explains the types of hyaluronic acid fillers, areas treated, and what to look for when choosing a practitioner.
keyTakeaways: Formulated with cross-linked Hyaluronic Acid (HA), a natural molecule that binds 1,000x its weight in water.
Restores youthful facial volume, sculpts cheekbones and jawlines, and hydrates the lips.
Non-surgical rhinoplasty offers dramatic profile straightening in under 30 minutes.
100% reversible using hyaluronidase enzyme for complete peace of mind.

body.heading: What Are Hyaluronic Acid Dermal Fillers?
paragraphs: Hyaluronic Acid (HA) is a naturally occurring glycosaminoglycan found throughout our skin, joints, and connective tissue. It is responsible for retaining moisture, maintaining skin suppleness, and providing internal cushion.

As we age from our mid-twenties, our bodies produce approximately 1% less hyaluronic acid annually. In aesthetic medicine, bio-identical cross-linked HA gels are used to replace lost deep fat pads, lift lax skin, and sculpt facial contours.

body.heading: Versatile Applications: Where Can Fillers Be Used?
paragraphs: Modern dermal fillers come in various rheological densities — from soft hydrating gels for delicate lips to firm structural gels for bone-mimicking projection:
bullets: Lips: Shaping, defining the vermilion border, restoring hydration, and adding balanced volume using Dr. Sofia’s refined Russian Lips technique.
Cheeks & Midface: Lifting sunken cheeks, restoring the youthful Ogee curve, and lightening nasolabial folds.
Tear Troughs: Filling hollow, shadowy under-eye circles to banish perpetual exhaustion.
Jawline & Chin: Sharpening mandibular definition, elongating the profile, and balancing facial symmetry.
Non-Surgical Rhinoplasty (Liquid Rhinoplasty): Camouflaging dorsal humps, lifting droopy nasal tips, and refining asymmetry without surgery.
Marionette & Smile Lines: Softening deep depressions around the mouth.

body.heading: Safety First: The Reversibility Advantage
paragraphs: One of the greatest safety assets of premium hyaluronic acid fillers is their complete reversibility. In the rare event that an adjustment is desired or an asymmetry arises, an enzyme called Hyaluronidase can be injected to safely dissolve the gel within hours.
At YourHealthFirst Clinic, we strictly use CE-marked, FDA-cleared premium brands, and all procedures are performed under stringent clinical sterility.

body.heading: Choosing the Right Practitioner in London
paragraphs: While dermal fillers are widely available, clinical outcome depends heavily on the injector's anatomical knowledge, aesthetic eye, and injection technique. Dr. Sofia utilizes blunt-tipped microcannulas wherever possible to minimize tissue trauma, bruising, and vascular risks, ensuring optimal patient comfort.

faqs.question: Does the dermal filler procedure hurt?
faqs.answer: Most patients experience only mild pressure. Premium fillers contain built-in lidocaine (a local anesthetic), and topical numbing cream is applied beforehand for your complete comfort.

faqs.question: When are results visible?
faqs.answer: Results are visible immediately! Minor swelling may be present for 24 to 48 hours, with the final settled result visible at two weeks.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Anti-Wrinkle injections and Dermal Fillers?
faqs.answer: Anti-wrinkle injections relax hyperactive muscles that cause dynamic expression lines. Dermal fillers restore lost physical volume and structural projection.
